newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast products steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast products steady in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline and diesel prices were steady in thin trade late Monday after firming earlier in the day, traders said.
Gains in the NYMEX complex spread to the West Coast spot market early in the day, although few deals were heard done as traders assessed their positions heading into the final weeks of the year.
"Trade in December is going to be quiet for most of the month," one trader said.

NYMEX January gasoline ended the day up 2.66 cents a gallon at a contract-high 68.12 cents, and front-month heating oil finished up 1.89 cents a gallon at 73.57 cents on supply concerns that rippled through the futures market.
Los Angeles regular unleaded gasoline was steady at 63.50 cents a gallon bid, 64.50 cents asked, and talked 4.0 cents weaker in the Bay Area, traders said.
Jet fuel was talked 73.50/74.50 in both markets.
